title: Heart failure: type, acuity and hypertension
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's heart failure and any related hypertension.
note:
Chief Complaint
Shortness of breath and increased swelling.

HPI
Pt is an 87 y/o female presenting for f/u of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. Pt reports worsening dyspnea on exertion and increased pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities over the past week. Pt states she has been feeling more fatigued. She denies chest pain or syncope. Pt has a hx of hypertension. Exam reveals increased peripheral edema compared to previous visit.

Medication List
Furosemide 40mg PO BID
Lisinopril 10mg PO daily
Amlodipine 5mg PO daily

Exam
General: Alert, in no acute distress.
CV: RRR, regular rhythm.
Lungs: Mild crackles at bases.
Extremities: 2+ pitting edema to mid-calf.
Vitals: BP 142/88, HR 78, RR 18, SpO2 95% on RA.

Assessment
1. Acute on chronic heart failure (HFpEF)
2. Hypertension

Plan
1. Increase furosemide dose to 80mg PO BID for acute exacerbation of heart failure.
2. Continue current HTN regimen.
3. Pt to monitor weight daily and call office if rapid weight gain occurs.
4. F/u in 2 weeks.

Electronically signed, R. Mensah, DO, 05/12/2026
explanations: Hypertension with heart failure is presumed linked: I11.0, hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, plus the I50 code.
Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure: I50.33 (HCC 224).

distractors.why: The classification presumes a causal link between hypertension and heart failure.
An acute exacerbation of chronic heart failure is documented (HCC 224).
It is acute on chronic, not a new acute heart failure.
